questions.q: Edo State government spends ₦2.4 billion to construct a new technical college and equip its workshops. This spending is best classified as
options: capital expenditure
public debt servicing
recurrent expenditure
statutory transfer
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure covers spending on durable assets such as buildings and equipment that yield benefits over several years. Constructing and equipping a college creates fixed assets, unlike recurrent expenditure on salaries and routine running costs.

questions.q: Kebbi State has total revenue of ₦54 billion. Its recurrent expenditure is ₦32 billion, capital expenditure is ₦18 billion and it makes a statutory transfer of ₦6 billion. What is its fiscal balance?
options: ₦4 billion surplus
₦4 billion deficit
₦2 billion deficit
₦2 billion surplus
questions.explanation: Total expenditure is ₦32 billion + ₦18 billion + ₦6 billion = ₦56 billion. Since revenue is ₦54 billion, expenditure exceeds revenue by ₦2 billion, giving a deficit.

questions.q: A cooperative in Nasarawa State owns a tractor, but most members still cultivate small scattered plots with hoes. Which factor best explains the limited use of mechanization by the members?
options: Low population growth in rural areas
High demand for farm produce
Availability of extension officers
Small and fragmented farm holdings
questions.explanation: Mechanization is economical when holdings are large and contiguous. Small scattered plots make tractor use difficult and costly, so many smallholders continue with manual tools.

questions.q: In Nigeria, which factor is most commonly responsible for the low capacity utilisation of many manufacturing firms?
options: Abundance of skilled labour
Unreliable electricity supply
Very low costs of production
Excess supply of locally produced raw materials
questions.explanation: Manufacturing firms often rely on costly generators because public electricity supply is unreliable, raising costs and limiting output. The other listed conditions would generally support, not constrain, production.

questions.q: A bakery in Abuja buys flour from Kano but locates its plant in Abuja. Which factor best explains this location decision?
options: Flour is a bulky raw material that loses weight in processing
Limestone deposits are needed for baking
The bakery depends mainly on iron ore from Abuja
Bread is perishable and costly to distribute over long distances
questions.explanation: Bakeries are market-oriented when the final product is perishable or bulky relative to the raw material. Locating in Abuja reduces delivery time and transport costs for bread, even though flour comes from Kano.

questions.q: A young entrepreneur in Aba wants medium-term finance to purchase industrial machinery for a small manufacturing firm but has limited collateral. Which institution is primarily established to provide such development finance in Nigeria?
options: Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives
Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation
Central Bank of Nigeria
Bank of Industry
questions.explanation: The Bank of Industry is the development finance institution focused on providing medium- and long-term finance to industrial enterprises, including manufacturing. The Central Bank regulates banking and monetary policy, while the NDIC insures deposits.

questions.q: The secondary market segment of the Nigerian capital market is important mainly because it
options: insures customers' deposits in failed banks
enables existing securities to be bought and sold, providing liquidity to investors
issues new shares to companies raising capital for the first time
fixes the interest rates that commercial banks charge borrowers
questions.explanation: The primary market handles new issues, while the secondary market allows investors to trade already-issued securities. This trading makes securities easier to sell before maturity and thus improves liquidity.

questions.q: The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation performs its primary function by
options: issuing currency notes and coins
lending directly to peasant farmers
fixing the exchange rate of the naira
insuring deposits in insured banks up to a statutory limit
questions.explanation: The NDIC protects depositors by providing deposit insurance in the event of bank failure, up to the statutory maximum. Currency issuance is done by the Central Bank of Nigeria, not the NDIC.

questions.q: In a given year, a country has visible exports of ₦18 trillion, visible imports of ₦15 trillion, invisible exports of ₦4 trillion and invisible imports of ₦5 trillion. What is its balance on the current account?
options: ₦2 trillion surplus
₦4 trillion surplus
₦2 trillion deficit
₦3 trillion surplus
questions.explanation: Total current receipts are visible exports ₦18 trillion plus invisible exports ₦4 trillion = ₦22 trillion. Total current payments are visible imports ₦15 trillion plus invisible imports ₦5 trillion = ₦20 trillion, so the current account surplus is ₦2 trillion.

questions.q: Country P can produce either 80 tonnes of groundnuts or 20 tonnes of rubber with the same resources, while Country Q can produce either 30 tonnes of groundnuts or 15 tonnes of rubber. Which statement is correct?
options: Country Q has a comparative advantage in groundnuts, while Country P has a comparative advantage in rubber
Country Q has a comparative advantage in rubber, while Country P has a comparative advantage in groundnuts
Neither country can gain from specialisation and trade because both can produce both goods
Country P has a comparative advantage in both groundnuts and rubber
questions.explanation: For Country P, 1 tonne of rubber costs 4 tonnes of groundnuts (80 ÷ 20), while for Country Q it costs 2 tonnes of groundnuts (30 ÷ 15); rubber is therefore relatively cheaper for Country Q. For groundnuts, Country P gives up only 0.25 tonne of rubber per tonne, compared with 0.5 tonne in Country Q, so Country P has the comparative advantage in groundnuts.

questions.q: The consumer price index of a country rose from 150 to 168 within a year. What was the inflation rate for the year?
questions.explanation: Inflation rate = ((168 − 150) ÷ 150) × 100 = (18 ÷ 150) × 100 = 12%. The value 18% comes from comparing the 18-point rise with 100 rather than with the initial index. Thus prices rose by 12% during the year.

questions.q: A trader in Kano keeps ₦250,000 as cash savings for one year. If the general price level rises by 25% over the year, what is the real value of the savings at the end of the year?
questions.explanation: Real value = money value ÷ price index relative to the base year = ₦250,000 ÷ 1.25 = ₦200,000. A 25% rise in prices means each naira now buys only four-fifths of what it bought before. ₦312,500 results from wrongly adding 25% to the money value instead of adjusting for its lower purchasing power.

questions.q: Which type of inflation is most likely to result from a sustained increase in workers' wages that is not matched by an increase in productivity?
options: Cost-push inflation
Demand-pull inflation
Hyperinflation
Imported inflation
questions.explanation: Wage increases not matched by productivity raise firms' costs of production, and firms may pass these costs on as higher prices. This is cost-push inflation. Demand-pull inflation arises mainly from excess aggregate demand rather than from rising production costs.

questions.q: The population of a state is 12,000,000. Of this, 7,000,000 are in the working-age group (15–64), while 4,200,000 are children under 15 and 800,000 are aged 65 and above. What is the dependency ratio?
questions.explanation: Dependants = 4,200,000 + 800,000 = 5,000,000, and the working-age population is 7,000,000. Dependency ratio = (5,000,000 ÷ 7,000,000) × 100 = 71.4%. The 140.0% figure is obtained by dividing the working-age population by dependants instead of the correct way round.

questions.q: A sachet water producer in Akure has fixed cost of ₦45,000 per month. She sells each bag of sachet water for ₦600, and the average variable cost per bag is ₦300. What is her break-even output per month?
options: 300 bags
75 bags
900 bags
150 bags
questions.explanation: Contribution per bag = selling price − average variable cost = ₦600 − ₦300 = ₦300. Break-even output = fixed cost ÷ contribution = ₦45,000 ÷ ₦300 = 150 bags. The 75 bags figure would wrongly divide fixed cost by the selling price instead of by contribution.

questions.q: A small firm has fixed cost of ₦20,000 and variable cost per unit of ₦80. It sells its product at ₦120 per unit. What is its profit when it produces and sells 600 units?
questions.explanation: Total revenue = 600 × ₦120 = ₦72,000. Total cost = ₦20,000 + (600 × ₦80) = ₦20,000 + ₦48,000 = ₦68,000, so profit = ₦72,000 − ₦68,000 = ₦4,000. Using contribution ₦40 per unit gives ₦24,000, but the ₦20,000 fixed cost must still be deducted.

questions.q: When the price of tea rises from ₦400 to ₦500 per packet, the quantity demanded of coffee rises from 80 to 96 packets. Using the simple percentage method, what is the cross elasticity of demand for coffee with respect to tea?
options: 0.2, and the goods are independent
0.8, and the goods are complements
0.8, and the goods are substitutes
1.25, and the goods are substitutes
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity of coffee = (96 − 80) ÷ 80 × 100 = 20%, while percentage change in tea price = (500 − 400) ÷ 400 × 100 = 25%. Cross elasticity = 20% ÷ 25% = 0.8; the positive sign shows that the goods are substitutes. The value 1.25 comes from dividing the price change by the quantity change.

questions.q: A consumer's monthly income rises from ₦60,000 to ₦75,000, and quantity demanded of beans rises from 40 kg to 44 kg. Using the simple percentage method, what is the income elasticity of demand for beans?
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = (44 − 40) ÷ 40 × 100 = 10%; percentage change in income = (₦75,000 − ₦60,000) ÷ ₦60,000 × 100 = 25%. Income elasticity = 10% ÷ 25% = 0.4. The value 2.5 wrongly divides the income change by the quantity change.

questions.q: If the price elasticity of demand for a commodity is 0.5, by how much will quantity demanded change if its price falls by 10%?
options: It will increase by 20%.
It will decrease by 20%.
It will increase by 5%.
It will decrease by 5%.
questions.explanation: Price elasticity = percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in price. Here 0.5 = percentage change in quantity ÷ 10%, so the quantity change is 5%. Since price falls, the quantity demanded rises by 5% because demand is inelastic.

questions.q: Amina's marginal utility from consuming a fifth cup of kunu is zero. What does this imply about her total utility from five cups?
options: It is at its maximum.
It is zero.
It is falling at an increasing rate.
It has become negative.
questions.explanation: Marginal utility is the change in total utility when one more unit is consumed. If the fifth cup adds no utility, total utility has reached its highest point before it starts to fall. Total utility can still be positive even when the marginal utility of the last cup is zero.

questions.q: A rise in the price of a loaf of bread causes a movement along the demand curve for bread. Which factor is directly responsible?
options: The price of a close substitute
Population size
The price of bread itself
Consumers' income
questions.explanation: A change in the good's own price changes the quantity demanded and is shown as a movement along its demand curve. Changes in income, substitute prices and population size shift the demand curve rather than cause a movement along it.

questions.q: Street lighting in a Lagos neighbourhood is often regarded as a public good because
options: it is consumed by only one household at a time
one person's use does not reduce its availability to others and non-payers cannot easily be excluded
its consumption can be charged per hour to each user
it is provided only by private firms for profit
questions.explanation: A public good is non-rival and non-excludable in consumption. Street lighting generally satisfies both conditions because many people can benefit at the same time and it is difficult to prevent non-payers from benefiting. The other descriptions are more consistent with private or club goods.

questions.q: In the short run, a firm in perfect competition earns abnormal profit. In the long run, what is the most likely outcome in the market?
options: A single firm takes over the market and price discrimination begins.
Existing firms reduce output and the market price rises permanently.
New firms enter, market supply rises and price falls until normal profit is earned.
The government fixes a minimum price to preserve the abnormal profit.
questions.explanation: Abnormal profit attracts new firms into a perfectly competitive market. As more firms enter, market supply increases, price falls and abnormal profit is competed away until firms earn normal profit in the long run.

questions.q: Why is a monopolist charging a single price likely to have marginal revenue below the price of its product?
options: To sell an additional unit, it must reduce the price on all units sold.
Its average revenue curve is perfectly horizontal.
It produces at a level where marginal cost is always zero.
It faces many close substitutes supplied by rival firms.
questions.explanation: A single-price monopolist faces a downward-sloping demand curve. Selling one more unit requires lowering the price, and because the lower price applies to all units, marginal revenue falls below price. A perfectly horizontal average revenue curve describes a price-taking competitive firm, not a monopolist.

questions.q: A cinema in Abuja charges adults a higher ticket price than students for the same film. For this price discrimination to work, the cinema must be able to
options: separate the two groups and prevent students from reselling tickets to adults
operate in a perfectly competitive market with many rival cinemas
sell the same quantity to both groups at the same marginal cost
set price below marginal cost for adults while covering average cost
questions.explanation: Price discrimination requires that the market can be divided into groups with different willingness to pay and that resale between groups is prevented. If students could easily resell tickets to adults, the higher adult price would be undermined. Perfect competition and pricing below marginal cost are not conditions for successful price discrimination.

questions.q: A firm's production function is Q = 5K^0.4 L^0.6. If both capital (K) and labour (L) are doubled, what happens to output?
options: It increases by more than double, showing increasing returns to scale.
It doubles, showing constant returns to scale.
It remains unchanged because the exponents sum to one.
It increases by less than double, showing decreasing returns to scale.
questions.explanation: Doubling both inputs gives 5(2K)^0.4(2L)^0.6 = 5 × 2^(0.4+0.6) × K^0.4L^0.6 = 2Q. Since output doubles when all inputs are doubled, the production function exhibits constant returns to scale. The sum of the exponents being one does not mean output remains unchanged.

questions.q: A tailor's short-run total product is TP = 30L − 2L² units of clothing, where L is the number of workers. What is the average product of labour when L = 5?
options: 20 units per worker
100 units per worker
10 units per worker
25 units per worker
questions.explanation: At L = 5, total product is 30(5) − 2(5²) = 150 − 50 = 100 units. Average product is total product divided by labour, so 100 ÷ 5 = 20 units per worker. The value 10 units per worker is the marginal product at that level of labour, not the average product.

questions.q: A country's real GDP rises by 5% in a year, but income inequality also worsens and access to healthcare falls for many citizens. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: Economic growth and development are the same thing, so the data are contradictory.
Neither economic growth nor development can have occurred.
Economic development must have occurred because real GDP increased.
Economic growth has occurred, but economic development may not have taken place.
questions.explanation: Economic growth refers to an increase in real output, while development includes improvements in welfare, equity, health and living standards. A rise in real GDP shows growth, but worsening inequality and falling healthcare access mean development may not have improved. Growth and development are related but not identical.

questions.q: Which measure is most suitable for describing how unequally income is distributed among households in a Nigerian state?
options: Consumer price index
Gini coefficient
Human Development Index
Poverty headcount ratio
questions.explanation: The Gini coefficient summarises the degree of inequality in income distribution, ranging from complete equality to complete inequality. The poverty headcount ratio measures the proportion below a poverty line, while the consumer price index measures changes in the general price level.

questions.q: In the market for sachet water in Ibadan, the cost of packaging materials rises at the same time that a public health campaign increases consumers' preference for sachet water. What is the most likely effect on the market?
options: Equilibrium price falls, and equilibrium quantity rises.
Equilibrium price remains unchanged, but equilibrium quantity falls.
Equilibrium price rises, but the change in equilibrium quantity cannot be determined.
Equilibrium price rises, and equilibrium quantity certainly rises.
questions.explanation: Higher packaging costs reduce supply, shifting the supply curve to the left, while the campaign raises demand, shifting the demand curve to the right. Both shifts put upward pressure on price, but the quantity change depends on the relative sizes of the shifts. Therefore only the rise in equilibrium price can be predicted with certainty.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha reduces the price of a commodity from ₦80 to ₦70. As a result, quantity demanded rises from 200 to 240 units. Using the simple percentage method, the price elasticity of demand in absolute terms is
questions.explanation: Using simple percentage changes, quantity rises by (240 − 200)/200 × 100 = 20%, while price falls by (80 − 70)/80 × 100 = 12.5%. The absolute elasticity is 20 ÷ 12.5 = 1.6. The value 0.625 results from inverting the percentage changes.

questions.q: Which of the following will shift the demand curve for chicken in Lagos to the right?
options: A rise in the price of chicken
An increase in the incomes of Lagos residents, if chicken is a normal good
The imposition of a tax on poultry farmers
A fall in the price of chicken feed
questions.explanation: An increase in income raises the demand for a normal good at every price, shifting the demand curve to the right. A fall in feed prices or a tax on farmers affects supply, while a change in the price of chicken is a movement along the demand curve.

questions.q: A country has a national income of ₦60 billion and a population of 15 million. Its per capita income is
options: ₦900 billion
questions.explanation: Per capita income equals national income divided by population: ₦60,000,000,000 ÷ 15,000,000 = ₦4,000. Multiplying the national income by the population instead of dividing gives a meaningless large amount, not per capita income.

questions.q: Transfer payments are excluded from national income because they
options: are made only by the federal government
always increase the value of exports
are paid only to unemployed persons
do not represent current production of goods and services
questions.explanation: Transfer payments such as pensions and allowances move purchasing power between people but are not payments for currently produced goods or services. Including them would overstate national income because they do not add to current output.

questions.q: The Federal Government of Nigeria plans total expenditure of ₦28 trillion and expects total revenue of ₦22 trillion. If nominal GDP is ₦140 trillion, the budget deficit as a percentage of GDP is approximately
questions.explanation: The budget deficit is ₦28 trillion − ₦22 trillion = ₦6 trillion. As a share of GDP, this is (₦6 trillion ÷ ₦140 trillion) × 100 = 4.29%, approximately 4.3%. Expressing the deficit as a share of expenditure would give 21.4%, but the question asks for the share of GDP.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as capital expenditure in Nigeria's public budget?
options: Construction of a new bridge by the state government
Payment of salaries of civil servants
Purchase of stationery for government offices
Payment of interest on public debt
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure is spending on assets or projects that add to productive capacity, such as constructing a bridge. Salaries, stationery and interest payments are recurrent expenses because they are for day-to-day running or debt service.

questions.q: The main purpose of establishing industrial estates in Nigeria is to
options: reduce the powers of local government councils
fix the prices of agricultural exports
ensure that all manufactured goods are imported
provide shared infrastructure and support services for manufacturing firms
questions.explanation: Industrial estates are set up to provide roads, power, water and other shared facilities that individual small firms may not be able to provide for themselves. This lowers production costs and supports manufacturing, rather than fixing export prices or promoting imports.

questions.q: The Cross River State government trains cocoa farmers in improved fermentation and drying methods. This measure is most likely to
options: reduce the demand for cocoa in world markets
raise the price of imported chocolate in Nigeria directly
increase the quantity of cocoa imported into Nigeria
improve the quality and market value of the cocoa produced
questions.explanation: Improved fermentation and drying raise the quality of cocoa beans, making them more attractive to buyers and increasing their market value. The measure affects the quality of locally produced cocoa, not directly the quantity imported or world demand.

questions.q: A farmer in Nasarawa State borrows ₦250,000 from a microfinance bank at a simple interest rate of 9% per annum for one year. The interest payable is
questions.explanation: Simple interest is calculated as principal × rate × time: ₦250,000 × 9/100 × 1 = ₦22,500. The amount ₦25,000 would correspond to a 10% rate, not 9%.

questions.q: Which of the following items is a liability of a commercial bank?
options: Loans granted to customers
Cash in the bank's vault
Customers' current account balances
Treasury bills held by the bank
questions.explanation: Customer deposits are funds the bank owes to depositors, so they appear as liabilities on the bank's balance sheet. Cash in the vault, Treasury bills and loans to customers are assets because they represent resources or claims owned by the bank.
